name: Reserve at South Creek
city: Englewood (mailing address); unincorporated Arapahoe County (Dove Valley)
headline: April Housing plans to resyndicate and rehab Reserve at South Creek, a 168-unit family complex in unincorporated Arapahoe County (Dove Valley), turning 99 market-rate units affordable so that 166 of 168 are income-restricted at 60% AMI; it is on CHFA's 2026 Federal 4% award list.
why_it_matters: It is a template for using a county housing authority special limited partnership (for a property tax exemption) plus county bond cap to convert market-rate units in an expiring tax credit property to permanent affordability, at no county cash cost.

status.label: Credits awarded; closing and rehab start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award (subject to change), Arapahoe County assigned $7,005,092 of its 2026 bond cap to CHFA for the deal (RES 26-075, RES 26-193), and the county board approved intent to form a housing authority special limited partnership (RES 26-034). Final partnership terms were to come back to the housing authority board later; I found no closing or construction record.

next_step: Watch Arapahoe County Housing Authority (Board of County Commissioners) agendas for the definitive special limited partnership agreements, which staff said would come back before closing.

key_numbers.meaning: Today 69 are restricted and 99 are market rate; after the deal all 166 restricted units are at 60% AMI.
About $29.2M over 10 years; CHFA marks it subject to change.
$7,005,092 of it is Arapahoe County's 2026 bond cap, assigned to CHFA; the rest is presumably CHFA/statewide cap (inferred).
Arapahoe County assigned this share of its 2026 private activity bond cap to CHFA for the deal, raised from $4,005,092 in August.

parties.name: Arapahoe County Housing Authority (ArCHA), governed by the Board of County Commissioners

background.text: This is a resyndication of an existing property: today 69 units are restricted at 60% AMI and 99 are market rate; the deal converts the 99 market-rate units so all restricted units serve households under 60% AMI.
April Housing presented the special limited partnership to the county commissioners sitting as the ArCHA board at the 2026 ArCHA annual meeting (study session, 2026-01-12).

On 2026-02-03 the Board of County Commissioners passed RES 26-034, approving intent to form a special limited partnership between ArCHA and April Housing for the project; staff said final terms would come back to the ArCHA board later.
Arapahoe County received 7 applications for its 2026 bond cap; staff ranked Reserve at South Creek first, citing Prop 123-eligible units at 60% AMI and the planned ArCHA partnership.
The county's news release says 69 homes will be preserved and 99 market-rate homes converted for households under 60% AMI, 'protecting affordability for the long term.'
Prior sale history: April Housing is the sponsor and the existing owner is not named in the county records used here; no acquisition price is public.
Arapahoe County 2026 limits (CHFA, HUD effective 2026-05-01): 60% AMI income limit is $60,480 for 1 person and $86,400 for 4; max rent $1,620 (1BR), $1,944 (2BR), $2,247 (3BR).

A Denver7 preview (about January 2026) quoted April Housing's head of preservation on 'longer term affordability' and said the company would apply to the state for tax credits and bonds, with a timeline that 'could be as fast as the end of the year.'

timeline.event: April Housing presents the partnership at the ArCHA annual meeting (BOCC study session)

County staff recommend $4,005,092 of 2026 bond cap for the project (study session)
BOCC passes RES 26-075 assigning $4,005,092 of county bond cap to CHFA for the project
Staff recommend raising the county cap for the project to $7,005,092 (study session)
BOCC passes RES 26-193 assigning $7,005,092 of county bond cap to CHFA for the project
Listed on CHFA's Federal 4% award report

discrepancies: Address: CHFA, the county bond reports and CHFA's LIHTC list say 15611 E Jamison Drive (Census geocodes it), while the RES 26-034 staff report and resolution say 14611 E. Jamison Drive; 15611 looks right and 14611 a typo (inferred).

City: CHFA prints Englewood and RES 26-034 says 'Centennial, Colorado in unincorporated Arapahoe County'; county bond reports and the Census put it in unincorporated Arapahoe County (Dove Valley CDP), so both city names are mailing names only.

Bedroom mix as relayed in the task brief (Studio 48, 1BR 72, 2BR 46) is off by one column: CHFA's table reads Studio 0, 1BR 48, 2BR 72, 3BR 46, which matches the county (48/72/48 for all 168 units) if the 2 unrestricted units are three-bedrooms (inferred, e.g. staff units).
Bond cap: county staff said the project needs $23,500,000 of bond cap; CHFA lists $21,029,987 of PAB.
Meeting date: a Denver7 preview said the housing authority would decide on January 27, but county records show the presentation on 2026-01-12 and the vote (RES 26-034) on 2026-02-03.
County 2026 bond cap total: the 2026-03-31 staff report says $8,233,226; the draft resolution says $8,223,226.
open_questions: Total development cost, year built, the current owner's purchase date and price, and the rehab scope are not in the public county or CHFA records used here.
Final partnership terms with the housing authority and the length of the new affordability covenant.
Equity investor and price, bond buyer or lender, GC, rehab cost per unit, relocation plan for current market-rate tenants who may not income-qualify.
